verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Tell Aaron: When you set up the seven lamps, they must shine toward the area in front of the lampstand."
Aaron did this. He set up the lamps so that they lit the area in front of the lampstand, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The lampstand was made of gold, hammered into shape from its base to its flower shapes. Moses had it made just like the pattern the LORD had shown him.
The LORD said to Moses,
"Take the Levites from among the people of Israel and make them clean.
This is how to make them clean: Sprinkle the water for washing away sin on them. Have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so make themselves clean.
Then have them take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. You must take a second young bull for a sin offering.
Bring the Levites to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and gather the whole community of Israel there.
Bring the Levites before the LORD, and the people of Israel will put their hands on them.
Aaron will present the Levites to the LORD as a wave offering from the people of Israel, so that they may do the LORD's work.
The Levites will put their hands on the heads of the bulls. Offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make the Levites right with God.
Have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons, and present them to the LORD as a wave offering.
In this way you will set the Levites apart from the rest of the people of Israel, and the Levites will belong to me.
After you have made them clean and presented them as a wave offering, the Levites may go in to do their work at the Tent of Meeting.
They are the ones from among the people of Israel who are given completely to me. I have taken them for myself in place of every firstborn son of the people of Israel.
Every firstborn in Israel, whether person or animal, is mine. On the day I struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, I set them apart for myself.
And I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.

From all the people of Israel, I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons. They will do the work for the people of Israel at the Tent of Meeting and help make them right with God, so that no disaster will strike the people of Israel when they come near the holy place."
Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel did with the Levites everything the LORD had commanded Moses about them.
The Levites made themselves clean from sin and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD, and made them right with God to make them clean.
After that, the Levites went in to do their work at the Tent of Meeting under Aaron and his sons. They did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses,
"This is the rule for the Levites: Men twenty-five years old or more will come to take part in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
At fifty years old they must retire from their regular work and stop serving.
They may help their brothers with their duties at the Tent of Meeting, but they must not do the work themselves. This is how you must arrange the duties of the Levites."
